I've fixed the CSS/PostCSS error. 

The issue was in `src/index.css` where `@import "tailwindcss";` preceded `@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@300;400;500;600&display=swap');`. When Tailwind processes its import, it injects many lines of CSS (causing the web font import to appear much further down at line 2461 in the processed file), which violates the CSS rule that `@import` statements must precede all other rules.

I swapped their order so that the Google Fonts import is at the very top of `src/index.css`, before `@import "tailwindcss";`. I then ran `npm run build` to verify the fix, and the vite build successfully compiled the CSS without throwing the PostCSS error.

In Tailwind v4, using `@import "tailwindcss";` is exactly the correct, standard, and fully optimized way to initialize Tailwind. 

Unlike Tailwind v3, which required importing specific layers (`@tailwind base`, `@tailwind components`, `@tailwind utilities`), v4 streamlines this into a single import. The new v4 engine is built to be highly optimized—it scans your project files dynamically and **only** injects the CSS that is actually used in your project into the final output. 

Because of this, `@import "tailwindcss";` is not "heavy" and won't bloat your application; it natively behaves just as an optimized build should. Your `src/index.css` is perfectly set up for Tailwind v4, and no changes are needed to break out the imports!

Yes, setting `--color-*: initial;` will definitely affect pasted HTML blocks if those blocks rely on standard Tailwind color classes (like `text-blue-500` or `bg-red-600`). 

Here are the specific implications:
- **Missing Colors:** Because the default color palette has been removed, any standard color utilities used in the pasted HTML will no longer work. 
- **Under the Hood:** Those standard color classes will either not be generated by Tailwind, or they will reference CSS variables that are now set to `initial`.
- **The Result:** If an end-user pastes HTML containing standard Tailwind colors, those specific colors won't show up on the page. 

If you want to support copy-pasting standard Tailwind snippets with their intended colors, you would need to keep the default color palette instead of setting it to `initial`.
